To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cryobiology of Sprague-Dawlley, Wistar, and Fischer 344 rat zygotes has been characterized and that the cryopreservation of these zygotes has improved using a new method that uses EG as the CPA and a Tp of -30°C.

the permeability of zygotes to water and the cryoprotective agent EG was determined and used to develop a cryopreservation protocol that resulted in the best cryosurvival of zygotes (61.2%), which was not significantly different from the nonfrozen control group (54.6%), and resulted in 100% of the fetuses developing normally.

1) the permeability of rat embryos to water and the CPAs EG, DMS0, and PG is very similar and is not affected by the presence of the CPAs, 2) the reflection coefficient is very high for these CPAs, 3) the activation energy for water permeability is 8.7 kcal/mol, and 4) cryosurvival is highest when embryos are plunged at −30°C in a solution containing 1.5 M EG
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the cryopreservation of zygotes from three rat strains.
improving the cryopreservation methods for rat embryos, which is essential for future studies on the development of new rat models.

improving cryopreservation methods for rat zygotes, with the ultimate goal of providing a cost-effective method to cryopreserve large numbers of embryos from a variety of genetic backgrounds for use in research and biotechnology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cryobiology of zygotes is similar to other mammalian cells and that the cryobiological parameters of rat zygote membranes are not significantly different from those of other mammalian cells.
the cryosurvivals and fetal development of zygotes from the three different genetic backgrounds are comparable to those of Sprague-Dawy zygotes cryostored using EG and plunged at −30°C.
the cryobiology of zygotes from three genetic backgrounds is very similar, and that a Tp of 30°C and EG is the most efficient method to cryopreserve these zygotes.

the use of EG as the CPA, a Tp of –30°C, and the use of the cryopreservation method described in this manuscript would be the most effective method for cryopreservation rat zygotes.
